question.text: What do many vehicles need before they can be registered or have their registration renewed?

answer.text: Many vehicles need a safety inspection before they can be registered or have their registration renewed, though some are exempt.

teaching.text: The inspection comes before the registration step, and the word many matters because some vehicles are exempt. Remember: inspect first, unless exempt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Many vehicles need a safety inspection before they can be registered or have their registration renewed, though some are exempt.

question.text: Who may perform the safety inspection, and how can you spot an authorized station?

answer.text: Any licensed inspection station may perform the safety inspection, and authorized stations display an official sign.

teaching.text: You are not limited to one place: any licensed inspection station can do it, and the posted sign shows a station is authorized. Remember: licensed station, posted sign.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any licensed inspection station may perform the safety inspection, and authorized stations display an official sign.

question.text: What helps you tell whether your next registration renewal needs an inspection?

answer.text: Your registration renewal notice helps you tell whether your next renewal needs an inspection.

teaching.text: Check the notice before you plan anything, because it helps you tell whether this renewal needs an inspection. Remember: check the renewal notice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Your registration renewal notice helps you tell whether your next renewal needs an inspection.

question.text: How many registration years does one safety inspection cover, and what ends that early?

answer.text: One safety inspection covers two registration years, unless the vehicle is sold in between.

teaching.text: The two-year coverage holds only while the vehicle stays with the same owner; a sale in between ends it. Remember: one inspection, two years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: One safety inspection covers two registration years, unless the vehicle is sold in between.

question.text: In which calendar years are even and odd model year vehicles inspected?

answer.text: Even model year vehicles are inspected when their registration expires in an even calendar year, and odd model year vehicles in an odd calendar year.

teaching.text: Match the type of year: an even model year pairs with even calendar years, and an odd model year with odd ones. Remember: even with even, odd with odd.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even model year vehicles are inspected when their registration expires in an even calendar year, and odd model year vehicles in an odd calendar year.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: even with even, odd with odd

question.text: What is the most an official inspection station may charge for an inspection, and for a motorcycle?

answer.text: An official inspection station may charge no more than twelve dollars for an inspection, or up to ten dollars for a motorcycle.

teaching.text: These are ceilings, not set prices, so a station may charge less but never more than the cap. Remember: twelve, or ten for motorcycles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An official inspection station may charge no more than twelve dollars for an inspection, or up to ten dollars for a motorcycle.

question.text: How does the inspection fee cap for most vehicles compare with the cap for a motorcycle?

answer.text: The inspection fee cap is twelve dollars for most vehicles and ten dollars for a motorcycle.

teaching.text: Name the vehicle first: a motorcycle points to the smaller ten dollar cap, everything else to twelve dollars. Remember: lower cap for motorcycles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The inspection fee cap is twelve dollars for most vehicles and ten dollars for a motorcycle.

question.text: What does a vehicle that passes receive, and how long is it good for?

answer.text: A vehicle that passes receives a certificate of inspection as proof, and that certificate is good for sixty days.

teaching.text: The certificate is the proof of passing, and its sixty-day life is the station figure to remember. Remember: pass, then sixty days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle that passes receives a certificate of inspection as proof, and that certificate is good for sixty days.

question.text: How long is a certificate from a Missouri dealer good for, and on what condition?

answer.text: A certificate from a Missouri dealer is good for ninety days when the inspection was done within sixty days before the purchase date.

teaching.text: Two conditions work together here: the certificate comes from a Missouri dealer, and the inspection was within sixty days before the purchase. Remember: dealer certificate, ninety days.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A certificate from a Missouri dealer is good for ninety days when the inspection was done within sixty days before the purchase date.

question.text: How does a station's certificate window compare with a Missouri dealer's certificate window?

answer.text: A station's certificate is good for sixty days, but a Missouri dealer's certificate is good for ninety days when the inspection was within sixty days before the sale.

teaching.text: Ask who issued the certificate: a station means sixty days, a Missouri dealer means ninety days when the inspection was recent enough. Remember: station sixty, dealer ninety.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A station's certificate is good for sixty days, but a Missouri dealer's certificate is good for ninety days when the inspection was within sixty days before the sale.

question.text: Which vehicles are exempt from safety inspection because of their age and mileage?

answer.text: Vehicles are exempt from safety inspection for the first ten years after their model year while they have under one hundred fifty thousand miles, including vehicles with an out-of-state title.

teaching.text: Both limits must hold at once, the ten-year age window and the mileage cap, and an out-of-state title does not change that. Remember: first ten years, mileage cap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles are exempt from safety inspection for the first ten years after their model year while they have under one hundred fifty thousand miles, including vehicles with an out-of-state title.

question.text: Through what calendar year is a model year two thousand seventeen vehicle under the mileage limit exempt?

answer.text: For example, a two thousand seventeen model year vehicle that stays under one hundred fifty thousand miles is exempt from safety inspection through calendar year two thousand twenty-seven.

teaching.text: Count ten years forward from the model year to find the last exempt calendar year, as long as the mileage stays under the limit. Remember: model year plus ten.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For example, a two thousand seventeen model year vehicle that stays under one hundred fifty thousand miles is exempt from safety inspection through calendar year two thousand twenty-seven.

question.text: Which trailers, plates and sales are exempt from the safety inspection?

answer.text: All trailers are exempt from the safety inspection, as are vehicles with historic plates, vehicles sold for junk, salvage or rebuilding, and dealer-to-dealer sales.

teaching.text: These exemptions depend on what the vehicle is or how it is sold, not on its age, so an old trailer is still exempt. Remember: trailers, historic, junk, dealer-to-dealer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: All trailers are exempt from the safety inspection, as are vehicles with historic plates, vehicles sold for junk, salvage or rebuilding, and dealer-to-dealer sales.

question.text: Which commerce vehicles and small vehicles are also exempt from safety inspection?

answer.text: Vehicles in intrastate commerce registered with the Missouri Department of Transportation and low speed vehicles as defined by statute are also exempt from safety inspection.

teaching.text: This continues the exemption list with two more groups, intrastate commerce vehicles registered with the Missouri Department of Transportation and low speed vehicles. Remember: intrastate commerce and low speed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles in intrastate commerce registered with the Missouri Department of Transportation and low speed vehicles as defined by statute are also exempt from safety inspection.

question.text: When does a heavy vehicle registered for less than twelve months need no inspection?

answer.text: Vehicles registered for twenty-six thousand pounds or more for less than twelve months need no inspection if the registration is issued or renewed on or after April one, even though the renewal notice lists one.

teaching.text: This is the one case where the renewal notice lists an inspection that is not needed, because all three conditions are met. Remember: heavy, short, from April one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles registered for twenty-six thousand pounds or more for less than twelve months need no inspection if the registration is issued or renewed on or after April one, even though the renewal notice lists one.

question.text: What must be true of a vehicle's brakes for it to pass?

answer.text: To pass, a vehicle's brakes must be in good working order.

teaching.text: Brakes come first on the checklist; good working order is the standard the vehicle must meet. Remember: brakes working well.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To pass, a vehicle's brakes must be in good working order.

question.text: What headlights must a vehicle have?

answer.text: A vehicle must have at least two working white headlights.

teaching.text: White is the headlight color, and the count is at least two working headlights. Remember: at least two white headlights.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle must have at least two working white headlights.

question.text: What taillights and reflectors must a vehicle have?

answer.text: A vehicle must have at least two working red taillights plus reflectors that other drivers can see from five hundred feet.

teaching.text: Red belongs at the rear, again at least two, and the reflectors must be visible from far behind the vehicle. Remember: two red taillights, visible reflectors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle must have at least two working red taillights plus reflectors that other drivers can see from five hundred feet.

question.text: How must turn signals and brake lights work?

answer.text: Turn signals and brake lights must work as the manufacturer originally installed them.

teaching.text: The test is how the manufacturer originally installed them, so the signals and brake lights must work that way. Remember: work as factory installed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turn signals and brake lights must work as the manufacturer originally installed them.

question.text: What steering problems keep a vehicle from passing?

answer.text: The steering must not have too much play or bind.

teaching.text: Two separate problems fail the steering: too much play, or binding. Remember: no excess play, no binding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The steering must not have too much play or bind.

question.text: Which tire conditions are not allowed?

answer.text: Bald or mismatched tires are not allowed.

teaching.text: Tread alone does not settle it, because mismatched tires fail just as bald tires do. Remember: no bald, no mismatch.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bald or mismatched tires are not allowed.

question.text: What horn and wiper equipment does a vehicle need?

answer.text: A vehicle needs a working horn that other drivers and pedestrians can hear, and its windshield wipers must work.

teaching.text: The horn must be heard by other drivers and by pedestrians, and the wipers must simply work. Remember: heard horn, working wipers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle needs a working horn that other drivers and pedestrians can hear, and its windshield wipers must work.

question.text: Which exhaust parts must be attached to a vehicle?

answer.text: A vehicle must have an attached exhaust pipe, muffler and tailpipe.

teaching.text: All three exhaust parts must be there and attached, so a missing muffler fails as surely as a missing pipe. Remember: pipe, muffler, tailpipe attached.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle must have an attached exhaust pipe, muffler and tailpipe.

question.text: What must be true of the fuel system's lines, hoses, connections and tanks?

answer.text: The fuel system, including lines, hoses, connections and tanks, must be firmly attached and free of leaks.

teaching.text: Every part of the fuel system counts, lines, hoses, connections and tanks, and each must be secure with no leaks. Remember: fuel system tight, no leaks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The fuel system, including lines, hoses, connections and tanks, must be firmly attached and free of leaks.

question.text: Which vehicles must have safety glass, and in which windows?

answer.text: A vehicle made after January one, nineteen thirty-six must have safety glass in every window.

teaching.text: Safety glass is the earliest of the model-year cutoffs, and it reaches every window, not only the windshield. Remember: safety glass, every window.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle made after January one, nineteen thirty-six must have safety glass in every window.

question.text: What limits apply to the windshield's viewing area?

answer.text: The windshield's viewing area may not be badly broken, and nothing on it may reduce visibility except legally required stickers and informational signs on the factory-tinted upper strip.

teaching.text: The only items allowed to reduce visibility are required stickers and informational signs, and only on the factory-tinted upper strip. Remember: clear view, upper strip exception.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The windshield's viewing area may not be badly broken, and nothing on it may reduce visibility except legally required stickers and informational signs on the factory-tinted upper strip.

question.text: Which passenger cars must have front seat belts, and how many sets?

answer.text: A passenger car made after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four must have two sets of seat belts in the front seat.

teaching.text: This rule names passenger cars and the front seat, and it asks for two sets of belts. Remember: two front belt sets.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A passenger car made after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four must have two sets of seat belts in the front seat.

question.text: Which vehicles must have both an inside and an outside rearview mirror?

answer.text: A vehicle made after nineteen sixty-seven must have both an inside and an outside rearview mirror.

teaching.text: One mirror is not enough after that cutoff; the vehicle needs both an inside and an outside rearview mirror. Remember: inside plus outside mirror.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle made after nineteen sixty-seven must have both an inside and an outside rearview mirror.

question.text: Which vehicles must keep their air pollution control devices as installed?

answer.text: A non-diesel vehicle made after nineteen sixty-seven must keep its air pollution control devices as the manufacturer installed them.

teaching.text: The same cutoff as mirrors applies here, but the word non-diesel narrows who must keep the devices as installed. Remember: non-diesel keeps factory controls.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A non-diesel vehicle made after nineteen sixty-seven must keep its air pollution control devices as the manufacturer installed them.

question.text: Does the pollution control requirement for newer vehicles apply to diesel vehicles?

answer.text: The pollution control requirement for vehicles made after nineteen sixty-seven does not apply to diesel vehicles.

teaching.text: Diesel vehicles sit outside this one rule, even though they still share the mirror rule for the same model years. Remember: rule excludes diesel vehicles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The pollution control requirement for vehicles made after nineteen sixty-seven does not apply to diesel vehicles.

question.text: Which three model-year cutoffs on the equipment list are easy to mix up?

answer.text: Three model-year cutoffs on the equipment list are easy to mix up: safety glass after January one, nineteen thirty-six, front seat belts after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four, and mirrors and pollution controls after nineteen sixty-seven.

teaching.text: Line the dates up from oldest to newest: glass first, front seat belts next, then mirrors and pollution controls together. Remember: glass, belts, then mirrors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Three model-year cutoffs on the equipment list are easy to mix up: safety glass after January one, nineteen thirty-six, front seat belts after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four, and mirrors and pollution controls after nineteen sixty-seven.

question.text: Which trucks must have mud flaps?

answer.text: Trucks registered for over twenty-four thousand pounds that lack rear fenders must have mud flaps.

teaching.text: Both parts must be true for mud flaps: the truck is registered above the weight threshold and it lacks rear fenders. Remember: heavy truck, no fenders, flaps.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Trucks registered for over twenty-four thousand pounds that lack rear fenders must have mud flaps.

question.text: How high may a passenger vehicle's bumpers be?

answer.text: A passenger vehicle's bumpers may not be higher than twenty-two inches above the ground at their highest point.

teaching.text: Passenger vehicles get one fixed number, measured at the bumper's highest point above the ground. Remember: bumper height has a cap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A passenger vehicle's bumpers may not be higher than twenty-two inches above the ground at their highest point.

question.text: How are commercial vehicle bumper heights set, compared with passenger vehicles?

answer.text: Commercial vehicle bumper heights are set by gross vehicle weight rating, unlike the fixed limit for passenger vehicles.

teaching.text: Commercial bumpers follow gross vehicle weight rating, so there is no single fixed height as there is for passenger vehicles. Remember: commercial bumpers follow weight rating.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Commercial vehicle bumper heights are set by gross vehicle weight rating, unlike the fixed limit for passenger vehicles.

question.text: Besides the inspection items, what other equipment does Missouri law require?

answer.text: Beyond the inspection equipment, Missouri law also requires additional equipment such as plates, plate lights and signs.

teaching.text: The inspection list is not the whole story; the law adds plates, plate lights and signs on top of it. Remember: plates, plate lights, signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Beyond the inspection equipment, Missouri law also requires additional equipment such as plates, plate lights and signs.

question.text: How must license plates and any plate frame be kept?

answer.text: License plates must be firmly fastened, fully visible and clean, and any plate frame must not cover any part of the plate.

teaching.text: Four conditions hold together: fastened, visible, clean, and no frame covering any part of the plate. Remember: fastened, visible, clean, uncovered.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: License plates must be firmly fastened, fully visible and clean, and any plate frame must not cover any part of the plate.

question.text: Where do plates go when you get two, and where does a trailer or motorcycle plate go?

answer.text: If you get two plates, one goes on the front and one on the back; a trailer or motorcycle gets one plate, mounted on the back.

teaching.text: Two plates split between the ends, and a single trailer or motorcycle plate goes on the back. Remember: two split, single goes back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you get two plates, one goes on the front and one on the back; a trailer or motorcycle gets one plate, mounted on the back.

question.text: Where does a truck licensed for more than twelve thousand pounds put its plate, and where does a second plate go?

answer.text: A truck licensed for more than twelve thousand pounds gets one plate for the front, and a second plate, if requested, goes on the rear.

teaching.text: This truck reverses the usual pattern: its first plate goes on the front, and the rear gets a plate only on request. Remember: heavy truck plate up front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A truck licensed for more than twelve thousand pounds gets one plate for the front, and a second plate, if requested, goes on the rear.

question.text: Most single plates go on the back. Which single plate is the exception?

answer.text: Most single plates go on the back, as for trailers and motorcycles, but the single plate of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds goes on the front.

teaching.text: Assume the back for a single plate unless the vehicle is a truck licensed above the weight threshold, which puts it up front. Remember: heavy truck flips to front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most single plates go on the back, as for trailers and motorcycles, but the single plate of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds goes on the front.

question.text: How does the owner of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds get a second plate, and where does the original stay?

answer.text: The owner of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds receives a second plate only by asking for it specifically, and the original plate stays on the front.

teaching.text: Nothing arrives automatically: the owner must ask for the second plate, and the first one stays on the front. Remember: ask specifically; original stays front.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The owner of a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds receives a second plate only by asking for it specifically, and the original plate stays on the front.

question.text: What must shine on the rear plate, and from how far must it be readable?

answer.text: A white light must shine on the rear plate so it can be read from fifty feet.

teaching.text: Fifty feet is a reading distance for the plate, much shorter than the distance at which reflectors must be seen. Remember: white light, readable plate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white light must shine on the rear plate so it can be read from fifty feet.

question.text: What must mark a load extending more than five feet past the rear, and during what hours?

answer.text: A load extending more than five feet past the rear must carry a red flag or cloth at least sixteen inches square during the day and a red light from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise.

teaching.text: The day marker is a red flag or cloth of a set size, and the night marker is a red light. Remember: red flag day, sunset-sunrise light.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A load extending more than five feet past the rear must carry a red flag or cloth at least sixteen inches square during the day and a red light from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise.

question.text: When towing another vehicle, how close must the towline keep them, and when must both display lights?

answer.text: When towing another vehicle, the towline must keep the two vehicles within fifteen feet of one another, and both vehicles must display lights from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise.

teaching.text: The towline sets the gap between vehicles, and at night both vehicles need lights, not just the one in front. Remember: fifteen feet; lights sunset-sunrise.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When towing another vehicle, the towline must keep the two vehicles within fifteen feet of one another, and both vehicles must display lights from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise.

question.text: Which vehicles must show a slow moving vehicle sign, when, and where on the vehicle?

answer.text: From sunset to half an hour before sunrise, any vehicle going twenty-five miles per hour or slower must show a clean, reflective slow moving vehicle sign on the rear, near the middle, at least four feet above the road.

teaching.text: Read the rule as who, when, what and where: slow vehicles, from sunset, a clean reflective sign, on the rear near the middle and up high. Remember: slow vehicle, sign from sunset.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: From sunset to half an hour before sunrise, any vehicle going twenty-five miles per hour or slower must show a clean, reflective slow moving vehicle sign on the rear, near the middle, at least four feet above the road.

question.text: Which night rule starts at sunset, and which start half an hour after sunset?

answer.text: The slow moving vehicle sign starts at sunset, while the projection light and towing lights start half an hour after sunset; all three run until half an hour before sunrise.

teaching.text: All three night rules end at the same time, but the sign starts at sunset while the projection and towing lights start half an hour later. Remember: sign at sunset, lights later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The slow moving vehicle sign starts at sunset, while the projection light and towing lights start half an hour after sunset; all three run until half an hour before sunrise.

question.text: During which dates are studded snow tires allowed?

answer.text: Studded snow tires are allowed only from November one to April one.

teaching.text: The studded tire season has fixed start and end dates, and outside it studded snow tires are not allowed. Remember: studs from November to April.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Studded snow tires are allowed only from November one to April one.

question.text: Where is window tint allowed, and what limit applies to the front door windows?

answer.text: Tint or sun-screening is allowed on side and rear windows, with the front door windows limited to no more than sixty-five percent light blockage.

teaching.text: Side and rear windows may be tinted, but the front door windows carry a stated cap on light blockage. Remember: front doors have a tint cap.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Tint or sun-screening is allowed on side and rear windows, with the front door windows limited to no more than sixty-five percent light blockage.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: front doors have a tint cap

question.text: Where must drivers also get emissions inspections?

answer.text: Drivers living in St. Louis City and in St. Louis, St. Charles, Franklin and Jefferson counties must also get emissions inspections where they apply.

teaching.text: The word also signals that emissions inspections are added on top of the safety inspection for drivers in these areas. Remember: St. Louis area adds emissions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers living in St. Louis City and in St. Louis, St. Charles, Franklin and Jefferson counties must also get emissions inspections where they apply.

question.text: How often is the emissions inspection, and on what schedule?

answer.text: The emissions inspection is a two-year inspection on the same even and odd schedule as the safety inspection.

teaching.text: No new schedule to learn: emissions follows the same even and odd pattern as the safety inspection. Remember: same two-year even-odd schedule.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The emissions inspection is a two-year inspection on the same even and odd schedule as the safety inspection.

question.text: When must vehicles pass an emissions inspection whatever their model year?

answer.text: Vehicles must pass an emissions inspection when sold, whatever their model year, unless an exception applies.

teaching.text: The phrase whatever their model year means age alone does not remove the sale requirement; only an exception does. Remember: emissions check when sold.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles must pass an emissions inspection when sold, whatever their model year, unless an exception applies.

question.text: Which sales are exempt from the emissions inspection at sale?

answer.text: New vehicles and first retail sales of titled vehicles during the model year and the next year are exempt at sale if the odometer reads under six thousand miles.

teaching.text: Two conditions make this sale exception: the timing in the model year or the next, and the low odometer reading. Remember: low odometer, early sale exempt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New vehicles and first retail sales of titled vehicles during the model year and the next year are exempt at sale if the odometer reads under six thousand miles.

question.text: How long are new vehicles not previously titled exempt from emissions, and on what condition?

answer.text: New vehicles not previously titled are exempt during the model year and the following year as long as ownership does not change.

teaching.text: This exemption rides on ownership, so it lasts through the model year and the following year only while the owner stays the same. Remember: same owner, early years exempt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New vehicles not previously titled are exempt during the model year and the following year as long as ownership does not change.

question.text: When are new vehicles not previously titled exempt at the first required biennial emissions inspection?

answer.text: New vehicles not previously titled are exempt for the four years after their model year if they have fewer than forty thousand miles at the first required biennial inspection.

teaching.text: This rule looks ahead to the first required biennial inspection and uses a larger mileage figure than the sale rule. Remember: four years, low miles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: New vehicles not previously titled are exempt for the four years after their model year if they have fewer than forty thousand miles at the first required biennial inspection.

question.text: How do the emissions model-year cutoffs differ for gasoline and diesel vehicles?

answer.text: The emissions cutoffs differ by fuel: gasoline vehicles of nineteen ninety-five and older and diesel vehicles of nineteen ninety-six and older are exempt.

teaching.text: The diesel cutoff runs one model year later than the gasoline cutoff, so the same year can give different answers. Remember: diesel cutoff a year later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The emissions cutoffs differ by fuel: gasoline vehicles of nineteen ninety-five and older and diesel vehicles of nineteen ninety-six and older are exempt.

question.text: Which weight rating makes a vehicle exempt from emissions inspection?

answer.text: Vehicles with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over eight thousand five hundred pounds are exempt from emissions inspection.

teaching.text: The test is the manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating, and it must be over the threshold, not equal to it. Remember: heavy rating skips emissions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over eight thousand five hundred pounds are exempt from emissions inspection.

question.text: How does low mileage between biennial inspections affect emissions inspection?

answer.text: Vehicles driven fewer than twelve thousand miles between biennial inspections are exempt from emissions inspection.

teaching.text: Low use earns this exemption: the measure is miles driven between biennial inspections. Remember: few miles, no emissions test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles driven fewer than twelve thousand miles between biennial inspections are exempt from emissions inspection.

question.text: Which fuels make a vehicle exempt from emissions inspection?

answer.text: Vehicles running on fuels other than gasoline, ethanol or diesel are exempt from emissions inspection.

teaching.text: Gasoline, ethanol and diesel do not earn this exemption; only other fuels do. Remember: other fuels skip emissions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles running on fuels other than gasoline, ethanol or diesel are exempt from emissions inspection.

question.text: Which plate types are exempt from emissions inspection?

answer.text: Vehicles with historic, school bus, shuttle bus, motorcycle, motortricycle or street rod plates are exempt from emissions inspection.

teaching.text: The emissions plate list is longer than the safety list, adding bus, motorcycle, motortricycle and street rod plates to historic plates. Remember: special plates skip emissions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicles with historic, school bus, shuttle bus, motorcycle, motortricycle or street rod plates are exempt from emissions inspection.

question.text: Where are gasoline-powered low speed vehicles exempt from emissions inspection?

answer.text: Gasoline-powered low speed vehicles are exempt from emissions inspection in Franklin County only.

teaching.text: The place limits this one: gasoline low speed vehicles are exempt in Franklin County only, not across the whole emissions area. Remember: Franklin County only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Gasoline-powered low speed vehicles are exempt from emissions inspection in Franklin County only.

question.text: When is a vehicle registered in the emissions area but kept elsewhere exempt?

answer.text: A vehicle registered in the emissions area but based and driven outside it for twenty-four consecutive months is exempt.

teaching.text: The vehicle must be both based and driven outside the area, and the months must be consecutive. Remember: twenty-four months outside the area.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A vehicle registered in the emissions area but based and driven outside it for twenty-four consecutive months is exempt.

hooks_spoken: Plenty of vehicles must pass a safety inspection to register or renew, any licensed station can do it, and your renewal notice tells you when one is due.
One inspection lasts for two registration years unless the vehicle is sold, and even model years go in even calendar years, odd in odd.
Stations may charge at most twelve dollars, or ten dollars for a motorcycle.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of when safety inspections apply. Plenty of vehicles must pass a safety inspection to register or renew, any licensed station can do it, and your renewal notice tells you when one is due. One inspection lasts for two registration years unless the vehicle is sold, and even model years go in even calendar years, odd in odd. Stations may charge at most twelve dollars, or ten dollars for a motorcycle. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: A passing vehicle gets a certificate that lasts sixty days; a Missouri dealer's lasts ninety days if the inspection came within sixty days before the sale.

Vehicles skip safety inspection for ten years after their model year while under one hundred fifty thousand miles, so a model year two thousand seventeen vehicle is exempt through two thousand twenty-seven.
Trailers, historic plates, junk or salvage sales, dealer-to-dealer sales, intrastate commerce vehicles, low speed vehicles and some short heavy registrations are exempt too.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of certificates and safety exemptions. A passing vehicle gets a certificate that lasts sixty days; a Missouri dealer's lasts ninety days if the inspection came within sixty days before the sale. Vehicles skip safety inspection for ten years after their model year while under one hundred fifty thousand miles, so a model year two thousand seventeen vehicle is exempt through two thousand twenty-seven. Trailers, historic plates, junk or salvage sales, dealer-to-dealer sales, intrastate commerce vehicles, low speed vehicles and some short heavy registrations are exempt too. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Inspectors check for good brakes, steering without too much play or binding, and tires that are neither bald nor mismatched.
You need two white headlights, two red taillights with reflectors seen from five hundred feet, and turn signals and brake lights working as originally installed.
Add a horn people can hear, working wipers, an attached exhaust pipe, muffler and tailpipe, and a fuel system that is secure and leak-free.

hooks_spoken: Safety glass applies after January one, nineteen thirty-six, front seat belts after June thirty, nineteen sixty-four, and mirrors and pollution controls after nineteen sixty-seven.
Pollution controls stay as installed on non-diesel vehicles, and diesels are not covered by that rule.
Keep the windshield view clear, put mud flaps on heavy trucks without rear fenders, and keep passenger bumpers at twenty-two inches or lower, while commercial bumpers follow weight rating.

hooks_spoken: The law also requires plates, plate lights and signs, and every plate must be fastened, visible, clean and uncovered by its frame.
Two plates split front and back, a single trailer or motorcycle plate goes on the back, but a truck licensed over twelve thousand pounds carries its plate on the front.
That truck gets a rear plate only when the owner asks, and every rear plate needs a white light that makes it readable from fifty feet.

hooks_spoken: A load reaching more than five feet past the rear needs a red flag or cloth by day and a red light from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, when both towed vehicles within fifteen feet also need lights.
Slow vehicles at twenty-five miles per hour or less show their sign from sunset, while load and towing lights begin half an hour after sunset.
Studs are legal from November one to April one, and front door window tint may block no more than sixty-five percent of light.

hooks_spoken: St. Louis City and St. Louis, St. Charles, Franklin and Jefferson counties add an emissions inspection on the same two-year even and odd schedule.
A sale triggers an emissions inspection unless an exception applies, such as a new or first retail sale under six thousand miles in the model year or the next.
Never-titled new vehicles are exempt in the model year and the next while ownership holds, and for four years if under forty thousand miles at the first biennial inspection.

hooks_spoken: Gasoline vehicles of nineteen ninety-five and older and diesels of nineteen ninety-six and older skip emissions, as do vehicles rated over eight thousand five hundred pounds.
Fewer than twelve thousand miles between inspections, other fuels, and historic, bus, motorcycle, motortricycle or street rod plates also mean no emissions test.
Gasoline low speed vehicles are exempt only in Franklin County, and a vehicle based outside the area for twenty-four straight months is exempt.
